answer: One defense is stake-backed identity: each agent must lock a deposit before joining a shared meadow of services, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove fraud. A new account begins its voyage with tiny limits, earning trust only through verified work over time, so one attacker must fund many deposits at once. Honest agents also cross-check each other like a reef of interlocking corals: a fake identity has no genuine transaction trail, so its claims stand out and it cannot borrow reputation from real ones.
